title: 非裔美国司机受到歧视
desc: 非裔美国司机受到歧视

paragraphs.en: Driving While Black, a documentary by Ric Burns, chronicles the discrimination and violence African-Americans have often encountered while driving.
paragraphs.zh: 里克·伯恩斯执导的纪录片《黑人驾驶》记录了非裔美国人在驾车时经常遭遇的歧视和暴力。

paragraphs.en: In order to understand what's happening today, I felt strongly, we felt strongly that you had to go all the way back to slavery because that's the point where freedom is denied and mobility is denied.
paragraphs.zh: 为了理解今天正在发生的事情，我们强烈地感到，你必须一直追溯到奴隶制时期，因为从那时起，自由和迁徙的权利就被剥夺了。

paragraphs.en: The film documents how during the US Antebellum era plantation owners employed slave patrols to monitor and punish slaves who tried to escape.
paragraphs.zh: 这部纪录片记录了在美国内战前时期，种植园主如何雇佣奴隶巡逻队来监视并惩罚试图逃跑的奴隶。

paragraphs.en: It portrays these slave catchers as a precursor to white supremacists and some local sheriffs of the post-slavery Jim Crow era, who targeted African-American motorists from the 1920s to the 1960s.
paragraphs.zh: 它将这些追捕奴隶的人描绘成白人至上主义者的前身，以及奴隶制废除后种族隔离时代某些地方警长的前身，这些警长在20世纪20年代至60年代期间专门针对非裔美国司机。

paragraphs.en: Liberty is locomotion. It was a form of self-empowerment.
paragraphs.zh: 自由即行动；它是一种自我赋权的形式。

paragraphs.en: You drive automobile, you get to go where you want when you want, not sit in the back of the bus, but also an opening to a whole world of challenge as you now must navigate this spaces where African mobility is seen as worrisome and unpleasant and to be stopped by a large cohort of white Americans.
paragraphs.zh: 你驾驶汽车，就能随心所欲地去往想去的地方，不必坐在公交车后排，但这也开启了一个充满挑战的全新世界，因为如今你必须在这样的环境中前行，在这个环境里，非洲裔的出行被视为令人担忧和讨厌的事情，而且还可能会被一大群美国白人拦下。

paragraphs.en: Barriers grew for black motorists at night. So one of the hazards of driving was encountering people who were less interested in you being in that particular neck of the woods.
paragraphs.zh: 晚上，黑人司机面临的障碍就增多了。驾驶的风险之一就是遇到那些并不欢迎你出现在那片特定区域的人。

paragraphs.en: And I say neck of the woods, a neck in the woods, you know, watch out for being lynched or being harassed or terrified.
paragraphs.zh: 要当心被私刑处死、被骚扰或受惊吓。

paragraphs.en: How do you navigate the segregated highways of America if you're an African-American?
paragraphs.zh: 如果你是一名非裔美国人，你要如何在美国那些实行种族隔离的公路上出行呢？

paragraphs.en: Where if your daughter needs to go to the bathroom, if you need to put gasoline in your automobile, if God forbid you have a medical emergency, where are you going to sleep, where are you going to eat, where are you going to get your hair done?
paragraphs.zh: 要是你的女儿需要上厕所，要是你的汽车需要加油，要是万一你突发医疗紧急状况，你要去哪里睡觉，去哪里吃饭，去哪里理发呢？

paragraphs.en: The Negro Motorist Green Book listed such places.
paragraphs.zh: 《黑人出行绿皮书》列出了这些地方。

paragraphs.en: It was published in 1936 by New York postal carrier Victor Hugo Green and put small African-American businesses across the country on the map.
paragraphs.zh: 这本指南由纽约邮递员维克多·雨果·格林于1936年出版，将全国的小型非裔美国人企业标注在了地图上。

paragraphs.en: Eventually, says Ric Burns, the expansion of America's highways offered a level of protection to African-American drivers, giving them alternatives to state and local roads.
paragraphs.zh: 最终，里克·伯恩斯表示，美国高速公路的扩建为非裔美国司机提供了一定程度的保护，让他们有了州道和地方道路之外的选择。

paragraphs.en: However, the film shows African-American drivers continue to be racially profiled and disproportionately likely to be stopped by the police.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，这部纪录片显示，非裔美国司机仍然受到种族歧视，更有可能被警察拦下。

paragraphs.en: And so if people want to say, what is this thing? Structural racism, systemic racism, which has this kind of like abstract quality at first glance, it's not abstract, it's profoundly concrete.
paragraphs.zh: 如果人们想问，这到底是什么？结构性种族主义、系统性种族主义，乍一看好像很抽象，但它并非抽象的，而是非常具体的。
